verified_findings.claim: The legal election transition is now pinned to Constitution No.2 (1952-07-07), Presidential/Vice-Presidential Election Act No.247 (1952-07-18), and Enforcement Decree No.659 (1952-07-18). This corrects the prior loose July-15/July-18 transition chronology by distinguishing Assembly passage/implementing work from promulgated election law.

Official/public-institution election sources identify four presidential candidates: Rhee Syngman, Cho Bong-am, Yi Si-yeong and Sin Hung-u. National Assembly-announced totals on August 13 were Rhee 5,238,769; Cho 797,504; Yi 764,715; Sin 219,696.

The 1952 election actor graph must include the vice-presidential contest independently. The National Assembly chronology records Ham Tae-yong 2,943,813; Yi Pom-sok 1,815,692; Cho Pyong-ok 575,260; Yi Gap-song 500,927; Yi Yun-yong 458,583; Chon Chin-han 302,471; Paek Song-uk 181,388; Chong Ki-won 164,907 among the reported totals.

Election-quality evidence is internally mixed and must remain decomposed: the US State Department later described the presidential election as seemingly free and uneventful, while NEC-commissioned scholarship discusses administrative intervention and the NIHK finding aid identifies observer photographs of anti-Cho material and damaged Cho campaign material. None alone proves nationwide uniform conditions.

The Liberal Party presidential and vice-presidential coalition was not a simple Rhee/Yi Pom-sok ticket. Muccio documented elite efforts against Yi before the election, and NEC-commissioned research records Rhee's support for independent Ham Tae-yong despite Yi being the Liberal Party vice-presidential candidate.

The Democratic Nationalist Party's October convention is evidence for the opposition's own retrospective interpretation of the election, including an allegation concerning Gwangju. It is not yet sufficient to create a verified Gwangju irregularity event without contemporaneous local administrative, police, press or court provenance.

adversarial_checks: State Department 'seemingly free and uneventful' wording is not a nationwide Korean election-quality finding.
NEC-commissioned retrospective discussion of administrative intervention must be traced to cited contemporaneous evidence before actor-level blame is assigned.
An anti-Cho poster photographed by observers proves existence at a photographed locality, not a nationwide centrally ordered campaign.
A defaced Cho poster proves damage to that campaign material, not the identity or chain of command of the perpetrator.
Rhee's support for Ham Tae-yong does not by itself prove a formal Liberal Party withdrawal of Yi Pom-sok.
Yi Pom-sok's poor relationship with other elites in Muccio's report is diplomatic observation, not a complete Korean opinion survey.
National Assembly announcement of totals establishes reported returns, not absence of local irregularities.
The compressed July 18 to August 5 election calendar is chronology and legal context, not standalone proof of fraud.
The Democratic Nationalist Party's October Gwangju allegation is opposition testimony requiring contemporaneous local corroboration.
FRUS intelligence about a later Cho Bong-am/Chang Myon coup faction is an intelligence report and must not be back-projected into the August campaign as established conduct.

limitations: The requested 40-document floor was not reached in the available execution window. NEC direct site access was partly blocked to automated retrieval, so searchable official NEC museum/research material and NIHK public archive descriptions were used without pretending inaccessible image originals were inspected. One vice-presidential candidate remains unidentified from the current official chronology excerpt. Search snippets were not counted as documents unless the underlying result exposed substantive document content.
